{{Short description|First large-scale and practical use of secure multi-party computation}}

The '''[https://www.partisia.com/docs/worlds-first-commercial-use-of-multi-party-computation-mpc/ Danish Sugar Beet Auction]''' was the first large-scale and practical application of [[secure multi-party computation]], which took place in January 2008.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last1=Bogetoft|first1=Peter|author-link1=Peter Bogetoft|last2=Christensen|first2=Dan Lund|last3=Damgård|first3=Ivan|last4=Geisler|first4=Martin|last5=Jakobsen|first5=Thomas|last6=Krøigaard|first6=Mikkel|last7=Nielsen|first7=Janus Dam|last8=Nielsen|first8=Jesper Buus|last9=Nielsen|first9=Kurt|last10=Pagter|first10=Jakob|last11=Schwartzbach|first11=Michael|date=2009|editor-last=Dingledine|editor-first=Roger|editor2-last=Golle|editor2-first=Philippe|chapter=Secure Multiparty Computation Goes Live|chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-642-03549-4_20|title=Financial Cryptography and Data Security|series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science|volume=5628 |language=en|location=Berlin, Heidelberg|publisher=Springer|pages=325–343|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-03549-4_20|isbn=978-3-642-03549-4}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Gomi|first=Kazuhiro|title=Council Post: Multi-Party Computation: Private Inputs, Public Outputs|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/forbestechcouncil/2021/10/26/multi-party-computation-private-inputs-public-outputs/|access-date=2021-11-11|website=Forbes|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2008-04-22|title=Nyt krypteret online-system regner på hemmelige tal|url=https://videnskab.dk/kultur-samfund/nyt-krypteret-online-system-regner-pa-hemmelige-tal|access-date=2021-11-11|website=videnskab.dk|language=da}}</ref> An electronic [[double auction]] was successfully run by a multiparty computation involving representatives of [[Denmark]]'s only [[sugar beet]]s processor ([[Danisco]]), the Danish sugar beet growers' association, and a research group responsible for implementing and running the computation.<ref name=":1" />

Due to [[European Union]] sugar market policy reforms which reduced sugar [[Subsidy|subsidies]] and lowered prices,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bogetoft|first1=Peter|last2=Boye|first2=Kristoffer|last3=Neergaard-Petersen|first3=Henrik|last4=Nielsen|first4=Kurt|date=1 March 2007|title=Reallocating sugar beet contracts: can sugar production survive in Denmark?|url=https://academic.oup.com/erae/article-abstract/34/1/1/2926658|journal=[[European Review of Agricultural Economics]]|volume=34|pages=1–20|doi=10.1093/erae/jbm002 |via=[[Oxford University Press]]|url-access=subscription}}</ref> as well as the recent closure of one of Danisco's sugar processing plants, the Danish [[sugar beet]] industry needed to reallocate production contracts to farmers nation-wide in an attempt to retain market efficiency. The decision made was to hold an electronic [[double auction]] to find the new [[Market clearing|market clearing price]] of sugar beets, where the role of the "auctioneer" was played by a computer program implementing a [[secure multi-party computation]] (SMPC) between the farmers and Danisco.

The use of SMPC not only reduced expenses of the [[auction process]] (when compared to hiring an external consultancy to run the auction), but also allowed farmers' bids to remain private from [[Danisco]], the only sugar beets processor on the Danish market and the seller of production contracts.<ref name=":0" /> This was important as farmers' bids can reveal their individual economic positions and productivities, which Danisco could have hypothetically used to their advantage when selling contracts. In a survey of the auction participants, 80% of respondents indicated that it was important to them that the bids were kept confidential.<ref name=":0" />

Aside from organizing the logistics of such a novel auction, the actual computation of the market clearing price and each bidder's positions only took about 30 minutes to complete.<ref name=":0" /> Ultimately, the auction resulted in the transfer of 25 thousand tons of production rights between farmers.<ref name=":0" />
